note: Opens with Kunti Moktan's pop-selo hit, Kutumba's instrumental, the genre's pioneer Hira Devi Waiba (HMV) and a 1996 cassette selo. The peak runs from instrumental tunes named Tamang Selo (sarangi, flute, folk bands) through the 2009-2010 Indreni cassette albums sung in Tamang to current singles. Most ties are by title: the track, or the album it is on, names the genre; Hira Devi Waiba, Navneet Aditya Waiba and Indira Gole Gurung are tied through their performer pages, Kunti Moktan through the Kathmandu Post.

size.basis: No source counts recordings; this is a judgement, not a count. What was read: Hira Devi Waiba, called the genre's pioneer, sang nearly 300 folk songs (Radio Nepal from 1966, HMV albums 1974 and 1978); Kathmandu cassette labels (Ranjana Music, Indreni Cassette Center, Music Nepal) issued Tamang selo albums from the 1990s on, several now on iTunes; established singers have a few selo albums each (Indira Gole Gurung: three); a damphu selo programme ran 100 episodes; and an iTunes US search for 'tamang selo' on 2026-11-23 returned more than 150 releases naming the genre, most of them single-track YouTube-era uploads from 2023-2026 (Raj Kumar Dong Tamang, Chitra Bahadur Tamang, Jivan Bomjan Tamang and others with a dozen or more each). Counting cassette-era albums, radio recordings and the stream of new singles gives a few thousand recordings; the high end allows for the large YouTube-only output. An insider's essential list is about 40: Hira Devi Waiba's early recordings, the 1990s pop-selo hits (Kunti Moktan's Mathi Mathi Sailungema), classic cassette selo singers and a handful of current stars.
